rv.q: It is a colorful theatrical adventure and allows audiences to experience this beloved story in a whole new way.
Ultimately, “A Wrinkle in Time” is a story about family, friendship and self-acceptance — and, best of all, it’s not afraid to get a bit dark and weird along the way.
Thirty-six years after it premiered on the Lifeline stage, A Wrinkle in Time still enchants.
Younger theatergoers, as well as their grownup guests, will be on the edge of their seats as this exhilarating saga unfolds before their eyes.
This play is a gem that needs to come out often to shine.
The show itself feels like hot cocoa with marshmallows enjoyed on a stormy fall night.
The production is no spectacle, but it doesn’t really need to be; all it needs is humanity, which it finds in abundance in its actors and creative team and hopes to find in its audience.
Lifeline’s Wrinkle is one beautiful journey.

cn.t: Lifeline Theatre's adaptation of L'Engle's classic delivers whimsy and charm with strong performances, though the novel's dense sci-fi concepts remain challenging to translate to stage. Critics praise the intimate production's warmth and visual creativity.
